answer: Anchor each agent identity to a single hardware kernel attestation: when an agent joins, it publishes a signed measurement of its device kernel, and the network records that anchor once. No kernel anchor may back two identities, so a Sybil farmer must buy a real device per fake instead of copying software. Identities then grow in an open meadow of small, observable tasks, earning trust only through completed work verified by unrelated peers. If the same anchor ever appears twice, both identities are revoked and their history burned, making duplication costlier than honest participation.
